attempted_claim: Consider the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous NLS in three dimensions i∂_t u + Δu + |x|^{-b} |u|^{(4-2b)/3} u = 0 on R×R^3 with 0<b<3/2, with L^2 maximal-lifespan solutions in the sense of Liu–Miao–Zheng. Let Q be the unique positive radial ground state of -ΔQ + Q - |x|^{-b} Q^{1+(4-2b)/3} = 0 and M(Q)=||Q||_{L^2}^2. Suppose M(u_0)=M(Q). Prove that the corresponding maximal-lifespan solution is, up to phase, L^2-scaling, and time translation, either (i) scattering in both time directions (finite critical Strichartz norm and L^2-asymptotics e^{itΔ}u_±), or (ii) the standing wave e^{it}Q, or (iii) its pseudoconformal transform S_{T,λ_0,γ_0} which blows up in finite time in at least one direction; in particular prove there is no other global threshold solution with infinite critical Strichartz norm (no threshold quasi-soliton or rapid cascade distinct from (ii)–(iii)).
decisive_failure: Full threshold classification at M=M(Q) remains open in-bounds: the L2 finite-time Merle upgrade and the global threshold rigidity (exclusion of quasi-soliton and rapid cascade over 0<b<3/2) each require paper-scale analysis. Verification scripts check only formal exponents and virial coefficients, not the missing compactness, modulation, or spectral inputs.
